newsitem.title: USA: Clinton defends U.N. veto decision backing Israel.
newsitem.headline: Clinton defends U.N. veto decision backing Israel.

text.p: President Bill Clinton on Monday defended the U.S. decision to veto a U.N. resolution condemning Israel for deciding to build housing in East Jerusalem but said it did not constitute U.S. approval of Israel's action.

Speaking at a news conference with Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak, Clinton told a questioner the United States felt the proposed U.N. criticism of Israel would have damaged efforts to promote Israeli-Palestinian peace negotiations. He added: "That should not be interpreted as an approval by the United States of the decision by the Israeli government."

Clinton said at the time of the Israeli decision to build more Jewish housing in Arab-dominated East Jerusalem that he opposed the move as a setback to peace efforts. But he nonetheless authorised as U.S. veto of a U.N. Security Countil Resolution condemning that view last week.

"I was very well aware of how the veto might make the United States look in the Arab world," he said during the White House news conference, with Mubarak standing by his side. But he asked Arabs to understand that "we have had a consistent position that we cannot achieve peace through U.N. resolutions."
Mubarak said he was "alarmed" by Israeli actions which he said tended to undermine peace efforts and specifically cited the East Jerusalem housing decision.

He referred to Clinton in warm terms as a partner for peace, but he also politely disagreed on the U.N. resolution issue, saying: "It is unfortunate that the resolution was not adopted because it may have given a signal to the Israelis to stop any settlement activies, especially in the area of Jerusalem, which is illegal. But I hope in the future we could avoid this."
